summary: Iteration 2 verification of Agency multi-tenant + real lead sourcing + encrypted credential vault on top of existing NEXUS build. Backend: 22/22 pytest passing (14 regression + 8 new). New coverage: Clients CRUD with computed leads/campaigns/connections counts; client-scoped leads and campaigns filtering; Integrations providers list (11 providers with fields+help); Connections encryption verified — GET /api/connections never returns plaintext secrets (only {set, hint:'••••XXXX'}), status transitions Pending→Partial→Connected across save calls, DELETE resets to Pending, client_id scope isolates connections from platform scope; Real lead scraping via /api/leads/scrape (stripe.com + notion.so, live HTTP, count>=1); CSV import maps 'title'→'role' and 'source' defaults to 'CSV Import'; empty CSV returns 400. Regression pass: auth (login/logout/me/register/unauth), strategy Groq JSON, content text + Gemini image (data URL), lead CRUD + AI score, sales assist, campaigns with derived CTR/CPC/CPA/ROAS/ROI, social generate/schedule/publish, analytics overview shape, agents list. Frontend E2E (real browser): admin login, top-bar active-client-select present, Clients page create + select client, Integrations page renders linkedin/sendgrid cards, sendgrid Configure modal saves credentials and status becomes CONNECTED, page HTML scanned — no plaintext SG.UI_TEST_SECRET leaked, Leads page Import CSV creates rows, score-lead-* triggers AI scoring which returns a numeric score with Warm category.

issues: Recharts still emits width(-1)/height(-1) warnings on initial mount — carried over from iteration_1, non-blocking.

critical_code_review_comments: secrets_store.py: Fernet key loaded once at import (module-level). If CREDENTIALS_KEY is missing, _fernet=None and encrypt() will raise AttributeError instead of a clean 500 with meaningful message. Consider raising on startup with a descriptive error.

server.py list_connections: q['client_id'] = client_id if client_id else None — this means when no client_id query is provided, only platform-scoped (client_id=None) connections are returned. Correct isolation, but this also means a client-scoped connection is invisible from platform view (which is the intended design and matches tests).

server.py save_connection ignores empty values for existing fields (preserves prior encrypted value). Good — allows 'leave blank to keep' UX. However it silently accepts unknown field keys and stores them; consider filtering to provider['fields'] only to prevent field-injection into stored dict.

leadsource._fetch uses synchronous requests inside asyncio.to_thread — OK for parallelism. Timeout is 15s per request and 4 candidates per domain — worst case ~60s per domain in bad network conditions; still bounded by 10 domains cap. Fine for MVP.
server.py leads/scrape stores every scrape result even when found=False (i.e., empty results). Currently accepted by tests (count>=1) but consider filtering s['found'] to avoid junk leads.
ObjectId(cid) in clients/connections/leads endpoints still not wrapped in try/except — malformed IDs will 500 instead of 400/404 (carried over from iteration_1).
server.py delete_connection uses client_id query param but does not validate provider exists; silently returns success — acceptable.
Test credentials file /app/memory/test_credentials.md is overwritten on every lifespan startup — good for keeping in sync with ADMIN_EMAIL/PASSWORD env values.
Frontend Integrations.jsx passes credentials as plain object over HTTPS to /api/connections — server encrypts at rest with Fernet. TLS is provided by ingress. Acceptable.
